bots.name: AddSearchBot
bots.description: Crawler for AddSearch's hosted site-search service. It indexes the pages of customer sites so AddSearch can serve search results for them, obeys robots.txt rules written for the AddSearchBot token, and AddSearch publishes the fixed addresses it crawls from for allowlisting.

bots.name: AdIdxBot
bots.description: Microsoft's crawler for Bing Ads / Microsoft Advertising. It crawls ads and follows through to the advertised landing pages for quality control, with both desktop and mobile variants.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 7_0 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/537.51.1 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/7.0 Mobile/11A465 Safari/9537.53 (compatible; adidxbot/2.0; +http://www.bing.com/bingbot.htm)

bots.name: Algolia Crawler
bots.description: Algolia's Crawler, which visits a customer's pages, extracts search-relevant content, and pushes it to Algolia search indices. Algolia documents a fixed User-Agent token and a single static egress IP address for allowlisting.

bots.name: Amazon AdBot
bots.description: Amazon's advertising crawler. It scans web pages that request ads from Amazon's advertising systems, collecting page content for Amazon's classification systems to maintain brand safety and improve ad relevance.

bots.name: Amazon Kendra Web Crawler
bots.description: The web crawler AWS runs for Amazon Kendra, its enterprise search service, which fetches the site URLs an AWS customer has configured as a data source and indexes them for that customer. Like the Bedrock knowledge-base crawler it is customer-directed but operator-run, and AWS states that customers must only point it at their own pages or pages they are authorised to index, and that using it to aggressively crawl sites the customer does not own is not acceptable use.

bots.name: AmazonProductDiscoverybot
bots.description: Amazon's product crawler, which collects publicly available product details from Amazon selling partner, brand and retailer websites to improve the accuracy and completeness of product information in Amazon's store. Amazon documents that it honours robots.txt user-agent and disallow directives, with changes taking up to 24 hours to apply, and that it does not support crawl-delay, nofollow or noindex. Amazon signs every request from this crawler with HTTP message signatures, publishing the Ed25519 key directory the Signature-Agent header points at.

bots.name: Amazon Q Business Web Crawler
bots.description: The web crawler AWS runs for Amazon Q Business, which fetches the websites an AWS customer has connected as a data source and indexes them into that customer's Q Business application. It is customer-directed but operator-run: AWS states the customer must only index their own webpages or webpages they have authorisation to index, and documents the robots.txt token site owners can use to allow or stop it.

bots.name: Amzn-SearchBot
bots.description: Amazon's crawler used to improve search experiences in Amazon products and services; Amazon states it does not crawl content for generative AI model training. Amazon publishes its source addresses on a dedicated page as a dated snapshot; they are recorded here verbatim.

bots.name: Anomura

The operator states it is not used to crawl content for model training, documents the robots.txt token Anomura, and publishes the addresses the crawler requests come from both on the page and as a JSON feed it says it will update if more are added.

bots.name: Applebot
bots.description: Apple's web crawler, used to index content for Siri, Spotlight Suggestions, and Safari's search features.

bots.name: Baiduspider
bots.description: Baidu's primary web crawler, fetching pages for Baidu Search indexing.

bots.name: Bublup Bot
bots.description: Bublup's content-discovery bot. It fetches pages to build the database behind Bublup's suggestion engine, reading page title, description and related images. Bublup states its crawling IPs are not fixed and documents reverse-DNS verification against the bublup.com domain instead.

bots.name: Channel3Bot
bots.description: Channel3's product crawler. It visits publicly accessible product detail pages and collects images, titles, descriptions, prices, availability and variants for Channel3's product catalogue, which AI apps and agents query to route shoppers back to the original site. The operator tells site owners not to hard-code its addresses and to verify it by forward-confirmed reverse DNS instead.

bots.name: Cludo
bots.description: Crawler for Cludo's hosted site-search product. It scans the domains a customer configures, follows links and sitemap URLs, and extracts page content and metadata into that customer's search index. Cludo documents that site owners can steer it with robots.txt rules addressed to the cludo token, and publishes the two proxy addresses — one per cluster, EU and US — that all of its services, crawlers included, make outbound requests from.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; cludo.com bot) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/148.0.7778.98 Safari/537.36

bots.name: coccocbot
bots.description: Cốc Cốc's web crawler, fetching pages for the Vietnamese Cốc Cốc search engine. Separate web and image sub-bots share the same verification domain.

bots.name: Daumbot
bots.description: Web-document crawler for Kakao's Daum search service in Korea. It collects pages so they can appear in Daum web search results, and Kakao's help centre states that the robot adheres to the robots exclusion standard when collecting documents from all sources, honouring both robots.txt rules written for the Daum token and noindex/none/nosnippet robots meta tags. The same help centre notes a blocked page's title can still appear in results when other pages link to it, because that text comes from the anchor text of the linking page rather than from a fetch of the blocked page.

bots.name: deepnoc
bots.description: Research crawler operated by deepnoc GmbH that parses and stores public web page content so that new search engines can query it without running their own crawling infrastructure. No IP ranges are published.

bots.name: Doofinder
bots.description: Fetcher for Doofinder's e-commerce site-search service. It retrieves the product data feed and page content of the shops that subscribe to Doofinder so their catalogue can be indexed for on-site search. The operator's security FAQ prints the user agent it sends and the three regional addresses it requests from, offering them as an alternative to putting credentials in a protected feed URL.

bots.name: DuckDuckBot
bots.description: DuckDuckGo's web crawler, used to improve DuckDuckGo's search results.

bots.name: ExaSearchBot
bots.description: Exa's search crawler, which discovers and indexes pages on the public web so that people and applications can find, retrieve and cite them through Exa. Every request is signed with HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421) under the Web Bot Auth scheme, so a request can be verified cryptographically regardless of its source IP address.

bots.name: FindFilesBot
bots.description: The crawler behind the FindFiles.net file search engine. It checks that publicly accessible files users search for are still available, using multiplexed HTTP/2 HEAD requests with a minimum ten-second interval per server, and may download images, videos and executables for classification and safety checks. Purpose-specific user agents are published for its link checking, favicon fetching, virus scanning and image classification agents, which all share one crawler host and address.

bots.name: FleebsBot
bots.description: Crawler for fleebs.com, a German real-time search engine. The operator's bot page documents two identities: one that searches for new information and one that analyses the pages it finds. It documents robots.txt blocking with the FleebsBot token and notes that pages indexed before a block may take time to drop out of the index.

bots.name: FreespokeCrawler
bots.description: Freespoke's search crawler, which fetches pages to build the index behind the Freespoke search engine. The operator documents the crawler's user agent, the robots.txt token FreespokeCrawler and support for the Crawl-delay directive.

bots.name: Geedo Product Search
bots.description: GeedoShopProductFinder is the crawler for Geedo, a product-search engine that indexes publicly accessible product pages from online stores and follows robots.txt rules.

bots.name: Google special-case crawlers
bots.description: A group of Google crawlers that operate under separate agreements between the crawled site and a specific Google product (AdsBot, AdSense, Google Safety scanning, and similar). Several members of this group ignore the wildcard robots.txt rule and must be targeted explicitly.

bots.name: Googlebot
bots.description: Google's primary web crawler, fetching pages for Google Search indexing.

bots.name: Googlebot Image
bots.description: Google's image crawler, which fetches images for Google Images and image features in Search. It is a distinct crawler from Googlebot with its own robots.txt token, though rules for Googlebot also apply to it.

bots.name: Googlebot Video
bots.description: Google's video crawler, which fetches video content for Google Search video features. It is a distinct crawler from Googlebot with its own robots.txt token, though rules for Googlebot also apply to it.

bots.name: GoogleOther
bots.description: Google's generic crawler family (GoogleOther, GoogleOther-Image, GoogleOther-Video), used by various Google product teams for fetching publicly accessible content. Robots.txt rules addressed to it do not affect Google Search.

bots.name: 360Spider
bots.description: 360Spider is the web-search crawler of 360 Search (so.com), the search engine operated by Chinese internet company Qihoo 360. The operator also runs 360Spider-Image and 360Spider-Video for image and video search.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1) AppleWebKit/537.1 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/21.0.1180.89 Safari/537.1; 360Spider

bots.name: IbouBot
bots.description: The crawler behind Ibou, a French conversational search engine. It discovers publicly accessible pages and indexes them so Ibou can cite and link back to the sites it answers from. The operator documents a 5-second politeness delay per host, publishes its address ranges as JSON, and documents forward-confirmed reverse DNS as the reliable way to tell a genuine request from a spoofed user agent.

bots.name: IONOS Crawler
bots.description: IONOS Crawler (IonCrawl) continuously crawls publicly accessible domains to generate insights into how they are used, which IONOS uses to improve and expand its hosting products. IONOS documents reverse-DNS verification and deletes crawled data after 60 days.

bots.name: Jooblebot
bots.description: The crawler for Jooble, a job-search aggregator that indexes job listings published across the web. Jooble's bot page states that it uses a web crawler which identifies itself as JoobleBot. No IP ranges are published.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Jooblebot/2.0; Windows NT 6.1; WOW64; +http://jooble.org/jooble-bot) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Safari/537.36

bots.name: Kagibot
bots.description: Kagi's web crawler, fetching pages for the paid Kagi search engine. Kagi publishes a fixed, small set of source IPs rather than a CIDR feed, each paired with a kagibot.org hostname.

bots.name: Linespider
bots.description: LINE's crawler. It fetches web pages to support LINE's search features and content services, and adheres to the Robots Exclusion Protocol outlined in robots.txt.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko; compatible; Linespider/1.1; +https://lin.ee/4dwXkTH) Chrome/W.X.Y.Z Safari/537.36

bots.name: LyonlBot
bots.description: The crawler used by Lyonl Search to discover and refresh public web documents for its index, with separate identities for web, image and news crawling so site owners can control each class independently. The operator documents robots.txt and crawl-delay support, conditional fetches with ETag and Last-Modified, and that the crawler does not submit forms or bypass authentication. It states that crawler address ranges are not currently published, so no verification recipe is recorded.

bots.name: MagnetmeBot
bots.description: Magnet.me's web crawler. It discovers and refreshes career-related pages — vacancies, events and employer information — for the Magnet.me careers platform. The operator documents that it may render JavaScript, follows the canonical version of a page, does not submit forms and adjusts its crawl speed automatically, and it publishes the addresses it crawls from as both a JSON and a plain-text list.

bots.name: Marginalia
bots.description: The crawler behind Marginalia Search, an independent search engine focused on older, text-heavy, and non-commercial web pages. Identifies itself by a bare URL rather than a conventional bot token.

bots.name: MetaJobBot
bots.description: MetaJobBot is the focused web crawler operated by the METAJob job meta-search engine. It searches websites for job listings to include in the METAJob index.

bots.name: MojeekBot
bots.description: Mojeek's web crawler, fetching pages for the independent Mojeek search engine index.

bots.name: MotoMinerBot
bots.description: MotoMiner's vehicle-listing crawler. It primarily crawls automotive dealership websites and adds their vehicle detail pages to the MotoMiner index. The operator documents robots.txt and crawl-delay support, honours bot-specific noindex meta directives, throttles outbound requests against defined traffic thresholds, and publishes the address the crawler currently requests from.

bots.name: Yeti
bots.description: Naver's web crawler, fetching pages for Naver Search indexing across South Korea's largest search engine. Naver documents two ways to confirm a request is really its search robot: a reverse-DNS lookup that resolves under naver.com, and a published JSON list of the IP ranges its search robots use.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko; compatible; Yeti/1.1; +https://naver.me/spd) Chrome/106.0.5249.0 Safari/537.36

bots.name: NestDaddyBot
bots.description: Web crawler behind the NestDaddy search engine. The operator's webmaster page documents that it extracts page title, meta description, headings, language and link structure to build the index, filters adult and abusive content out of results, and fully respects robots.txt including the Crawl-delay directive. It states that the crawler runs from a distributed network whose current ranges are available only on request.

bots.name: Openindex Spider
bots.description: Openindex operates a web-crawling cluster (Apache Nutch on an Apache Hadoop cluster) for research and development of universal and focused search engines. The crawler respects robots.txt and the Crawl-delay directive and identifies itself in the User-Agent.

bots.name: Paqlebot
bots.description: Paqle's news crawler. It indexes news articles to discover who is mentioned in the media, crawling at most one page per minute per site and tuning its rate to how often a site publishes. Paqle documents that the crawler falls back to a site's Googlebot robots.txt rules when no Paqlebot rules are present, and that its addresses reverse-resolve under paqle.net.

bots.name: PetalBot
bots.description: Huawei's web crawler, fetching pages for the Petal Search engine used in Huawei's mobile services and for Huawei Assistant content recommendations. Huawei documents reverse-DNS verification against aspiegel.com and petalsearch.com hostnames.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 7.0;) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Mobile Safari/537.36 (compatible; PetalBot;+https://webmaster.petalsearch.com/site/petalbot)

bots.name: PiplBot
bots.description: PiplBot is the web-indexing crawler operated by Pipl, an identity and people-search service. It retrieves and indexes publicly available information, including content behind searchable databases, to build Pipl's people-search index.

bots.name: Quantcastbot
bots.description: Quantcast's advertising crawler. It crawls websites to extract page content for interest-based audience categorization and to run quality-assurance checks on advertisement landing pages.

bots.name: Qwantbot
bots.description: Qwant's web crawler, fetching pages to build and refresh the index that powers the privacy-focused Qwant search engine. Qwant runs it under two documented forms — the plain crawler and a Qwantbot-news variant dedicated to Qwant News — and the user agent carries a worker id identifying the machine that made the request. Older crawls identify as Qwantify.

bots.name: SeekportBot
bots.description: The crawler for the Seekport search engine, operated by SISTRIX (Bonn, Germany). It fetches pages to build Seekport's search index and follows the Disallow directives in robots.txt.

bots.name: SemanticScholarBot
bots.description: SemanticScholarBot is the crawler for Semantic Scholar, an academic search engine built by the Allen Institute for AI. It crawls the web to find scholarly PDFs and metadata for indexing.

bots.name: SeznamBot
bots.description: Seznam's web crawler, fetching pages for the Seznam.cz search engine used primarily in the Czech Republic. Seznam publishes the full list of addresses the crawler uses as JSON, and documents that every SeznamBot address carries a fulltextrobot-*.seznam.cz reverse-DNS record.

bots.name: Site Search 360
bots.description: Crawler for the Site Search 360 hosted site-search product, operated by Zoovu (Germany) GmbH, formerly SEMKNOX. It indexes the pages of the customer sites it is pointed at, following links from the configured root domains and skipping external hosts. Robots.txt is not applied automatically: the control panel offers a "Fill Blacklist from robots.txt" action that imports a site's disallow rules into the crawl blacklist, and the crawler honours noindex robots meta tags. The operator publishes the addresses it crawls from for firewall allowlisting.

bots.name: Sogou Spider
bots.description: Sogou Spider is the web crawler for Sogou, a major Chinese search engine (owned by Tencent). It crawls and indexes web pages, news, and images to build Sogou's search index.

bots.name: stepstoneCrawlBot
bots.description: The Stepstone Group's job-listing crawler. Its crawler page states that it processes only publicly available information, observes robots.txt directives and keeps intervals between requests to avoid loading servers, and publishes the user agent it sends for transparency.

bots.name: StractBot
bots.description: The crawler for Stract, an open-source search engine. Stract documents the crawler's user agent and robots.txt behavior but publishes no IP list or reverse-DNS verification method.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; StractBot/0.2; open source search engine; +https://stract.com/webmasters)

bots.name: Swiftbot
bots.description: The web crawler behind Swiftype's site-search product, now operated by Elasticsearch B.V. Unlike a general search-engine crawler it only visits sites that Swiftype customers have asked it to crawl, in order to build a search index for those sites. The operator documents that Swiftbot obeys every restriction it finds in robots.txt, including a full-site disallow, and that it looks for the token Swiftbot.

bots.name: TinEye
bots.description: TinEye-bot is the web crawler operated by TinEye, the reverse image search engine built by Idee Inc. It crawls the web to discover and index images for TinEye's image-matching search service.

bots.name: TrovitBot
bots.description: Trovit's web crawler, which discovers new and updated pages to add to the Trovit classifieds search index. Trovit documents that it does not fetch most sites more than once per second and that it can be blocked with the trovitBot robots.txt token.

bots.name: urlsuma
bots.description: Crawler for urlsuma.de, a German general-purpose web search engine under construction. The operator documents that it re-reads robots.txt without caching before every single fetch, makes about two requests per visit (robots.txt plus one page), executes no JavaScript, and treats a 4xx response as a permanent block. Current crawler addresses are shared on request only.

bots.name: Webzio
bots.description: Crawler for Webz.io (formerly Webhose.io), a web-data provider that collects publicly available content to build structured data feeds. Webz.io publishes no IP ranges, so requests cannot be verified.

bots.name: WepchSearchEngine
bots.description: The crawler for Wepch, an independent privacy-focused search engine still in development. Its operator page states the project's purpose, gives a contact address for crawl complaints, and documents the robots.txt token site owners can use to crawl-delay or disallow it.

bots.name: Yahoo! Slurp
bots.description: Slurp is Yahoo Search's web crawler. It crawls and indexes pages for Yahoo Search results and also gathers content for Yahoo News, Finance, and Sports.

bots.name: Yahoo! JAPAN Crawler
bots.description: Web crawler operated by Yahoo! JAPAN (LY Corporation) to collect pages for its Japanese search index and related services. It identifies itself with Y!J-prefixed user-agent tokens and follows the Robots Exclusion Protocol.

bots.name: YandexBlogs
bots.description: Yandex's blog-search robot. Yandex's robot table documents it as the blog search robot that indexes post comments, and lists it as following robots.txt directives.

bots.name: YandexComBot
bots.description: Yandex's indexing robot for content in languages other than Russian, feeding the international yandex.com search index. Yandex's robot table documents that it can index content when there is no explicit robot-specific restriction, and lists it among the robots that do not follow the general robots.txt rules written for arbitrary robots.

bots.description: Yandex robot that loads resources such as JavaScript and CSS needed to render pages during crawling for Yandex Search.

bots.name: YandexVideo

bots.name: YandexBot
bots.description: Yandex's primary web crawler, fetching pages for Yandex Search indexing.
